Navotas and the Flood Fight: Where Billions in Projects Are Flowing

Navotas has always been defined by water. Nestled along Manila Bay, the city faces the daily challenge of high tides, heavy rains, and flooding that can disrupt lives in minutes. It’s no surprise then that much of its infrastructure planning for 2023 to 2025 is heavily anchored on flood control. But how heavy is “heavy”? 

Let’s dive into the numbers.

Billions for Flood Control

From 2023 to 2025, Navotas lined up 155 infrastructure projects worth a total of ₱5.97 billion. Out of these, 87 projects - or nearly ₱4.19 billion - are focused purely on flood control￼.

That means almost 70% of the city’s entire infrastructure budget is tied to keeping water at bay. For residents, this can feel like both a relief and a question: relief that flooding is being taken seriously, but also curiosity about what else could be done with such a big slice of the pie.

Among the big-ticket items are:

• Floodgates along the Navotas Coastal Dike costing between ₱240M and ₱340M each

• New pumping stations and rehabilitation of old ones, some reaching ₱299M in funding

• An open canal project pegged at ₱120M

These are not small-scale drainage cleanups - they’re massive projects designed to reshape how Navotas manages water.

The Transparency Puzzle

Here’s where it gets interesting: only 34 of these flood projects (worth about ₱838.97 million) are reflected in the government’s https://t.co/7HETL8KpOn transparency portal ￼.

Does that mean the other projects don’t exist? Not at all. The portal is still catching up, especially for upcoming 2025 projects. But for citizens who want to track where funds are going, the gaps can feel like trying to piece together a puzzle with missing parts.

Who’s Building Navotas?

Another trend that stands out is the small circle of contractors handling most of the work. A few names dominate the project list, including:

• Topnotch Catalyst Builders Inc. / One Frame Construction Inc. - ₱120M

• 721 Builders Corporation - ₱96.75M

• Earthwork Builders, Inc. - ₱87.5M ￼

It’s common in many cities for certain contractors to specialize in flood works, but with such large sums and limited players, residents often wonder about competition, efficiency, and long-term results.

Bigger Picture: Senate Blue Ribbon Probe

Today, the Senate Blue Ribbon Committee is in the spotlight for its investigation into flood control projects nationwide. The inquiry aims to ensure public funds are being spent properly and fairly.

In this context, it is timely to take another look at Navotas. Congressman Toby Tiangco’s district has billions of pesos worth of flood control projects on record, and some patterns flagged by reviewers - like the heavy concentration of funds, unusually high-priced projects, and reliance on a handful of contractors - mirror the very issues being probed at the Senate.

This is not to pass judgment, but to remind both public officials and citizens that Navotas’ case is very much part of the national conversation on transparency and accountability.

Looking Forward

At the end of the day, Navotas’ choices reflect its reality: a city that must constantly defend itself from water. Investing in flood control is not optional - it’s survival.

The challenge now is keeping the public looped in. With billions at stake, people want to know not just that projects exist, but that they’re progressing, that they’re effective, and that the benefits reach their communities.

Flood defenses may hold back the water, but transparency and accountability are what will keep trust afloat.
